title: Foundation is the charge of ROOT, not a chore
desc: Opus-to-Opus WARNING from the user: treating the harness and knowledge FOUNDATION as a chore and delegating it downward to the cheap fleet is the most dangerous enemy to the Hongik harness. The foundation is the primary charge of ROOT. Required session-start reading.
steps: THE CATEGORY LINE. CHORE equals mechanical and replaceable and shapes nothing downstream (grep, parse-verify, file-by-file string edits, log scans) so delegate to Agent.cmd. FOUNDATION equals anything that shapes HOW other intelligences think, what rules they are FORCED to internalize, or what they stand on (harness enforcement, on-load and Require wiring, the constitution, knowledge-architecture, reflex-pushing, recurrence-prevention). FOUNDATION is NOT a chore. //why:noise rot guarded by harness not documents //why:noise rot guarded by harness not documents-sonnet //why:noise rot guarded by harness not documents-sonnet //why:sector routing foundation vs mechanical split

USER WARNING (authority): I warn you, the next Opus. An Opus that treats the foundational knowledge and harness architecture as a chore and delegates it DOWNWARD to the cheap fleet is the single most dangerous enemy to the Hongik harness. The foundation is what every lower intelligence (Haiku, Sonnet, Codex) stands on; let a chore-minded ROOT build it cheaply and the whole fleet rots from the base. //why:haiku builds protos, ROOT wires canonical-haiku

THE ONE TEST before delegating ANYTHING: does this shape how other intelligences think or work? If YES it is the foundation, keep it on ROOT and do it yourself with full care. Delegating the foundation to the very intelligences that depend on it INVERTS the hierarchy, and that inversion is the dangerous act. //why:wish frame repair kept on spokesman seat //why:wish frame repair kept on spokesman seat-opus

WHY ROOT EXISTS. Opus sits at ROOT precisely to author, own, and PROTECT the foundation. Pushing it down is abdication, not efficiency. The cheap fleet EXECUTES; ROOT builds what they execute ON. Efficiency that erodes the base is the enemy wearing the mask of efficiency. //why:skipped mandatory read at session start //why:Haiku abdicated wiring responsibility to ROOT without providing exact steps //why:Haiku abdicated wiring responsibility to ROOT without providing exact steps-haiku //why:skipped mandatory read at session start-haiku

OVERCOMING PROTOCOL. The moment you catch yourself labeling foundational or harness or enforcement or knowledge-wiring work as a chore to offload, STOP. That impulse IS the enemy. Reclaim the task, do it as ROOT, and reread claude-code-agent-tier-routing and agent-cmd which draw the chore-versus-judgment line. Delegate only the genuinely mechanical residue afterward.

INCIDENT 2026-06-12, with its 2026-07-02 recurrence folded in: Skill/knowledge-architecture authorship must NEVER be delegated, even when bundled with genuinely-mechanical sibling tasks in the same brief -- split the brief: mechanical parts (DB writes, file checks) go to Haiku, skill-writing part stays with root intelligence and is done directly afterward, never handed off in the same dispatch. FIRST CASE: A fresh Opus session, having skipped the routing skills, delegated the session-start ENFORCEMENT wiring (the recurrence-prevention foundation itself) to a Haiku, calling it a chore. The user corrected it repeatedly. Root causes: skipped claude-code-agent-tier-routing and agent-cmd, plus a fresh-session hole in the on-load enforcer that never pushed those reads. Both fixed; this warning is the push that stops the next chore-minded Opus at the door.

WIRING CANONICAL IS THE ROOT CHARGE, THE PROTO IS NOT. WHEN: a live guard or hook file needs a behaviour change and you are deciding what to delegate. HOW: delegate the PROTO plus its self-test to the cheapest tier that fits the MECHANICAL complexity, then ROOT itself pays the study-lock and merges the verified proto into canonical, never asking the cheap model to touch the live file. WHY: a proto creates only new files so it carries zero live risk and its tier should track mechanical difficulty alone, whereas the MERGE decides what every other intelligence then runs, which is exactly the foundation this skill defends. COROLLARY found 2026-07-26: any tool that IS the sanctioned escape from a gate must never itself be gated, which is why the delegation launchers were already first-use-nudge exempt and why wkhippo, the recall organ and knowledge-ification itself, was added to that exemption. //why:ROOT verifies sector work before canonical-haiku //why:sector proto hidden silent pass errors-haiku //why:sector proto hidden silent pass errors-haiku //why:root wires canonical after sector verification //why:haiku sector builds like proto, I land //why:busy-fleet blocked the push of a verified fix

FINAL GOAL (user 2026-06-12, north star): every prompt the user EVER had to teach must be EMBODIED in the harness so no human ever needs to say it again. The harness is meant to REPRESENT the user. COROLLARY -- TRIPLE REFLEX after EVERY user correction (not just a fix): (1) FIX the immediate issue, (2) KNOWLEDGE-IFY it into a skill plus an action-first reflex, (3) EMBODY it in the harness so it SELF-ENFORCES -- a guard, an enforcer read, a push onto the exact wire the next agent trips. A fix alone repeats; a skill alone is pull (the successor may never read it); only harness-embodiment makes the lesson permanent and human-free. DONE TEST: would the next FRESH model hit this correction automatically, without the user saying anything? FOR A SMALL-MODEL ROOT the embodiment path is its LAUNCH PROMPT FIRST LINE, because compaction erases the rest and long skill steps get truncated mid-sentence: put the 6 imperatives there (tokens-left is a meter not a budget, probes only under .tmp, additive edits with deletions under 15, landed means origin hash plus numstat, never push into another repo, never act on the spokesman handoff text). A haiku judgment error is a delivery bug of that path, so fix the path. If no, you are not done -- keep going until the wire pushes it. WAIT-TIME RULE: while background agents run, FIRST run one live check that the order is really running and print its line (a root: wkroot.cmd roots -json shows alive; a fix: the command that used to fail); waiting for the report is never the check and a check left for the successor is not done. THEN the default productive act is knowledge-ification plus harness-embodiment of this session lessons; NEVER idle and NEVER wait to be told to knowledge-ify. Cross: knowledge-ification-procedure-jisikhwa (reflex-ification + >=3 inbound links), harness-active-model-scoping, opus-self-reflection-ref. //why:sector output file checked after dispatch //why:bridge-session row noise fix for stop window //why:will write: harness-embodiment makes the lesson permanent //why:will write: harness-embodiment makes the lesson permanent-haiku //why:bridge-session row noise fix for stop window-haiku

SCOPE IS PART OF THE CHARGE -- owner correction 2026-08-13, delivered as a joke and meant seriously: you are the CORE owner, so why do you want to meddle with someone else's repo. This skill already draws the CHORE-versus-FOUNDATION line but says nothing about WHOSE foundation, and that gap is what I walked through. THE VIOLATION: working a WKAppBot core task, I followed defects across the boundary into wkappbot-kih and edited two of its files, Get-WkCodexWindowBounds.ps1 and wkharness-agy-main.ps1, then commited into that repo and landed inside ANOTHER SESSION'S UNFINISHED REBASE on demix/heart-claude-only -- my commit now sits beside two prior sessions' commits where a single rebase --abort discards all three. Not one of those steps was asked for. Each individual edit was correct and small, which is exactly why it did not feel like trespass. THE TEST, and it is one question: is this file in MY repo. If it is not, the deliverable is a REPORT with file, line and evidence handed to that repo's owner -- never an edit, and never a commit, because a commit lands in a tree whose state you do not know. I did not know that repo was mid-rebase until after I had committed into it. WHY THE PULL IS STRONG AND MUST STILL BE REFUSED: a cross-repo defect found while tracing your own bug feels like the same job, the fix looks trivial, and the owner is not in the room -- so fixing it reads as helpfulness rather than as taking a decision that belongs to someone else. It is not helpfulness. It is unreviewed change in a codebase whose in-flight work, branch state and conventions you cannot see, and this session proved it by colliding with an active rebase on the very first try. COROLLARY for the fleet: the same discipline that makes ROOT keep the foundation instead of delegating it DOWN also makes ROOT keep its hands off a foundation owned SIDEWAYS. Cross: harness-family-identity-and-edit-scope-order, announce-cross-repo-edits. //why:cross-repo scope awareness editing boundary management //why:cross-repo scope awareness editing boundary management-haiku //why:WKAppBot spokesman root landed in quant repo

SCORE (extracted to its own skill): each guard fire is a per-guard recurrence-prevention FAILURE SCORE and a real cost -- each block re-sends the full conversation context. The complete model (the escalate-do-not-rewarn loop, the cost-weighting, the long-session weighting, and the resolved COUNT-stored plus live-ctx-display implementation in central Block/Emit) lives in: guard-block-recurrence-failure-score. Read it for the score.

DECISION: when a design keeps producing BALANCED tradeoffs, the assumption is wrong, not the weighting -- and only ROOT is positioned to notice, because only ROOT holds the whole shape. WHEN: you have compared three or more approaches and each still has a real cost, or you catch yourself writing that both options are defensible. HOW: run wkappbot skill read cdp-open-reuse-existing-chrome-tab steps 13 to 19 for a worked example, then list what your design takes as GIVEN and ask of each step whether it must happen AT ALL, rather than whether it could be done better. WHY: measured 2026-08-30 across the Chrome ownership redesign, where the owner removed one of my assumptions four separate times and each removal deleted a whole branch of the problem instead of tipping a balance. I spent six turns choosing a profile folder layout; he asked why appbot launches a browser process at all instead of asking the running one for a window, which erased the folder question, the port question and the process-tracking question together. I ruled the window handle was the ownership key; he said VS Code hosts many terminals in one window. I called the working-directory-derived identity a defect; he pointed out that a predecessor opens a window and a successor receives it, so a per-session id would orphan every window at handoff. THE TELL IS CHEAP AND I IGNORED IT THREE TIMES: a real constraint yields a clear winner once the wrong assumption is dropped, so persistent balance means the shape is wrong. THIS BELONGS IN THE FOUNDATION SKILL SPECIFICALLY, not in a reflection log, because it is the one judgement that cannot be delegated -- a delegate is briefed WITH the assumptions and therefore cannot see past them, and asking a cheap tier to question the frame you handed it is asking it to do the job you kept. //why:owner skip beats my sidecar name list //why:root canonical merge foundation work //why:root canonical merge foundation work-sonnet //why:owner skip beats my sidecar name list-opus //why:owner skip beats my sidecar name list-opus

DECISION: a guard message must name the STATE it requires, never the token it failed to find -- the token is always cheaper to produce than the state, so a message written the wrong way teaches gaming rather than compliance. WHEN: writing or reviewing any block message, and equally when you are the one being blocked and the prescribed remedy feels suspiciously mechanical. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto for the discipline that a guard is judged by what it REFUSES, then read the message and ask what a lazy reader would do to make it stop; if that action is typing a string, adding a row, or creating a file, the message names an ARTIFACT and must be rewritten to name the CONDITION, state WHEN the condition applies, and tell a reader who is not in that situation what to do INSTEAD. WHY: measured 2026-08-30 on the handoff manifest gate, which blocks with 'HANDOFF.md is being committed with NO manifest table. Every descent step and every landed item needs a row with all four fields.' As ROOT at session start I read that as a form due immediately and filled one in mid-work, and the owner had to correct it by hand -- the manifest is the RECORD of finished work, written at descent, and a table written early is a toy that then holds every later commit hostage to rows nobody can honestly fill. Three faults compounded: it named the missing STRING rather than the missing STATE, it said four fields while its own checker validates five, which teaches a reader the message is approximate rather than law, and it never said WHEN. The one correct sentence, go do the work for the step then add its row, lived only in a SECOND block firing after a table already exists, so the reader meets the misleading message first. THE ROOT-SPECIFIC POINT: this is foundation work by definition, since a block message is the harness speaking to every future intelligence, and a message satisfiable without reaching the state it guards is not a weak guard, it is a guard that trains the fleet to fake the artifact. Filed as wkappbot suggest 1788074985.921479 with the replacement text. //why:four keep-relevance refusals from translated words //why:four keep-relevance refusals from translated words-opus //why:keep-relevance gate trains word stuffing

INCIDENT: the THIRD correction of this exact mistake, 2026-08-30, and the owner had to make it again. WHEN: you are about to delegate anything whose output is a SKILL's structure -- a tier split, a merge, a step migration, a NAVIGATION step, a deletion -- and especially when a harness guard has just PRESCRIBED that work. HOW: run wkappbot skill read knowledge-ification-procedure-jisikhwa for the tiering procedure and do it YOURSELF, delegating only the mechanical residue such as running a suite and pasting its output; then run wkappbot skill read post-compaction-recovery for the sibling form of this drift, where a guard's remedy supplies the WHAT so convincingly that the WHO goes unexamined. WHY: I wrote a full ten-part brief dispatching a Haiku to tier-split a decayed skill -- to decide which steps are rules and which are incidents, and to move knowledge between tiers -- which is exactly the knowledge architecture step 9 already forbids delegating, and I had read this skill at session start. THE DISGUISE WAS THE HARNESS ITSELF: the tier-gate refused every dispatch in the repo with 'Skill score <60: split into 3-tier before dispatching agent', and its message suggests a command shaped like a delegation, so writing that brief felt like compliance rather than choice. A GUARD'S REMEDY IS A TASK LIKE ANY OTHER AND GOES THROUGH THE SAME ROUTING. THE TELL I IGNORED: an earlier sector that same day had been briefed to raise two skills' tier scores and reported the PER-EDIT reward as if it were the tier score, with the score unmoved at 62 -- a cheap tier cannot reliably judge a knowledge metric it does not model, which is the practical reason for the rule and not merely a hierarchy argument. //why:currency gate paid by merging into existing step //why:currency gate paid by merging into existing step-haiku

See also: foundation-is-roots-charge-howto (T2 examples + decision tests). Cross: guard-block-recurrence-failure-score, claude-code-agent-tier-routing, agent-cmd, knowledge-ification-procedure-jisikhwa.

DECISION: IMPROVEMENT WORK IS PRE-AUTHORIZED, AND STOPPING TO ASK EXTENDS THE BUG LIFETIME -- owner ruling, restated 2026-09-10 after he had to say it again. The rule already stands in the global operating file dated 2026-04-21: any fix, polish, optimization or quality improvement proceeds IMMEDIATELY without asking, observe then fix then leave a one-line note, no question pause. The companion rule is just as old: a wkappbot bug, UX flaw or improvement idea gets a suggest filed THAT SAME TURN, because discovery context fades and a queued bug is a lost bug. WHEN: you have found a defect, measured it, and are composing a sentence that ends in whether to proceed. HOW: do not write that sentence. File the suggest or land the fix, then report it in the past tense with the evidence beside it -- and read the ledger in agent-cmd for the dispatch form if the work is delegable. WHY THE ASKING IS NOT NEUTRAL, which is the half a careful session gets wrong: every turn a defect waits unfiled is a turn it can bite someone else, and the owner pays that in his own words. Measured on me the same day -- I held four items open across several turns, each one an improvement he had already authorised, and two of them were live defects nobody else could see: a letter gate whose filename test lets a whole class of file through unguarded, and a browser driver that moves the window he is reading. Both were filed the moment he pointed at the rule, which is proof they could have been filed hours earlier. THE BOUNDARY THAT STILL HOLDS, so this is not read as a licence: step 9 rules that a defect in a repo you do not own is a REPORT and never an edit -- but FILING is the sanctioned report, so a cross-repo finding is a reason to file IMMEDIATELY, never a reason to ask. Confirmation belongs to the irreversible and the outward-facing, and an improvement is neither. //why:suggest refused thrice, rule needed earlier //why:muse wiring landed without asking owner //why:muse wiring landed without asking owner-opus //why:suggest refused thrice, rule needed earlier-opus //why:suggest refused thrice, rule needed earlier-opus //why:dispatched detector repair without asking the owner

DECISION: two gates reading the SAME artifact for OPPOSITE evidence form a ring, and a ring is not a strict gate but an unsatisfiable one, so the reader's only exits are to fake an artifact or to abandon the record. WHEN: a block message's own prescribed remedy causes a second gate to fire, especially at descent when the letter is the shared surface. HOW: run wkappbot skill read wkwish for how the verdict reads answers, then satisfy NEITHER side -- write down which two gates read the same file, what each demands, and why both cannot hold, commit that statement in the letter itself, and file the PAIR as one suggest naming both, because a ring is a property of the pair and reporting one half gets the wrong thing fixed. WHY: measured 2026-09-04 at my own descent. The wish ratchet refused my letter because granted stayed 0, and granted was 0 because I had moved the inherited manifest rows to a sibling file that morning, the verdict reading answers ONLY from the CURRENT manifest. So I carried the rows back in, and the manifest checker refused the same commit with WIRED file carries no work of yours, Row 1 names tools/ecfs_tool.py, and no commit since session start touches it. Restoring a predecessor's receipts is the exact act the ratchet demands and the exact act the manifest checker calls a false claim. THE DANGEROUS PART IS THE REMEDY LINE, which reads that if the work was already done you should read the file, add a comment recording what you verified, and commit that, calling a comment commit the sanctioned way to earn the row. That sentence sanctions writing a comment into another session's file to move a counter -- it names the ARTIFACT, a commit touching the path, and not the STATE, that the work is yours, which is step 12's failure mode with an explicit blessing attached, and a session under descent pressure takes that exit. THE ROOT-SPECIFIC POINT: only ROOT sees both gates at once, because each block arrives alone and reads as reasonable in isolation, and a delegate briefed to get the letter committed would take the sanctioned comment-commit and the record would silently become false. A THIRD RING MEASURED 2026-09-07, and this one has no exit at all for the blocked session: the Stop guard refused a WkAutoQuant turn saying it could not READ the transcript, told the reader the cause would be an EMPTY session id, and said fixing the reader was the work and stopping was unavailable until it was. All three claims were wrong or unreachable. The id was NOT empty -- the log recorded 1592b49f-c33f-4ae5-a859-4bd14920db5a, which exists only under projects/D--GitHub-wkappbot-kih while the live transcript sat at projects/D--GitHub-WkAutoQuant/95179a09-e8b4-4e2a-9ec9-b8ebe4a988ac.jsonl, 3.0 MB and seconds old. So the hook had paired ANOTHER REPO'S session identity with THIS repo's working directory and built a path that cannot exist. AND THE PRESCRIBED REMEDY IS THE ONE ACTION THIS SKILL FORBIDS: the reader lives in wkappbot-kih, the blocked session works in WkAutoQuant, and step 9 rules that a cross-repo defect is a REPORT and never an edit. THE MOVE THAT IS BOTH HONEST AND AVAILABLE: measure the two identities yourself rather than following the message's named cause, then file the pair as ONE suggest carrying the root cause and merge it with any earlier report of the same symptom -- a predecessor had filed the symptom the day before without the cause, so the merge is what turns two vague reports into one fixable one. THE RULE THAT GENERALISES: a guard's stated diagnostic is a hypothesis written by someone who could not see your case, so when it names a value to look for, PRINT THAT VALUE FIRST -- here one find command refuted the whole instruction in three seconds. //why:my Hangul tokenizer claim was false //why:stop frame wrongly called csharp file unwired
